3:## [1.6.1] - 2026-11-25
4-
5-### Breaking Changes
6-
7-- Tool parks are tagged: `{ kind: "sleep", checkpoint?, until?, signals? }` and `{ kind: "wait", checkpoint?, on, policy }`, flat, in place of `{ sleep: { ... } }` and `{ wait: { ... } }`; a result has no `kind`. An object with another `kind` is an invalid park. Migration: return `{ kind: "sleep", ...sleep }` or `{ kind: "wait", ...wait }`, and tell a park from a result by `returned.kind`.
8-- `Wrap` is tagged: `{ kind: "tool", tool, wrap }` or `{ kind: "section", section, wrap }`. Migration: build wraps with `wrapTool()` and `wrapSection()`, or add the `kind`; read the target after checking `wrap.kind`.
9-- `onYield` hook results are tagged: `{ kind: "continue", continue }` or `{ kind: "tasks", tasks }`. Migration: add the `kind`. A task's `YieldDecision` (`{ continue? }`) is unchanged.
10-- `beforeCompact` hook results are tagged: `{ kind: "decline" }` or `{ kind: "summary", summary }`, in place of `{ decline: true }` and `{ summary }`. Migration: return the tagged forms.
11-- `Conversation.submit(tx, draft)` and `ConversationHandle.submit(tx, draft)` are `admit(tx, draft)`; `submit(draft, context)` is unchanged. Migration: rename the transaction form's calls to `admit`.
12-- `SignalState` is tagged: `{ kind: "value", value }` or `{ kind: "expired" }`, in place of `{ value }` and `{ expired: true }`. Migration: test `state?.kind === "value"` or `state.kind === "expired"` instead of `"value" in state`. Stored signal memos keep their shape.
13-- `CommitResult` (`Storage.commit()`) is tagged: `{ kind: "stored", stored }` or `{ kind: "refused", stored, refused }`. Migration: a custom Storage returns the tagged forms; a caller reads `refused` after checking `result.kind === "refused"`.
14-
15-### Fixed
16-
17-- Fixed `NodeExecutionEnv` on Windows not finding Git for Windows installed outside Program Files and running commands through the WSL launcher `System32\bash.exe` instead. It now asks the `git.exe` on `PATH` for its installation (`git var GIT_SHELL_PATH`, Git 2.47+) and uses its Git Bash before other `bash.exe` on `PATH` ([#12408](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12408))
18-- Fixed the Node environment's text line reader rescanning an incomplete line after every read, which made long lines take time quadratic in their length ([#12224](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12224))

20-## [1.6.0] - 2026-11-20
21-
22-### Breaking Changes
23-
24-- `RunEndTask` and `runEndTask` are renamed `HookTask` and `hookTask`, as `afterTools` and `onYield` hooks now ask for tasks too. Migration: rename the import in `afterRun` hooks.
25-- A tool's `execute()` returns `Promise<ToolExecutionResult | ToolPark>`: it may park instead of returning a result. Code that calls a tool's `execute()` itself, such as a wrapper or a test, handles parks; reading a result field still compiles, since a park has none. Code that annotates `Promise<ToolExecutionResult>` widens the annotation.
26-- `until` is optional on sleeping task states (`TaskState`, `TaskInspection`, `TaskGraphState`): a sleep may wait for signals only. Code that reads `until` of a sleeping task handles its absence.
27-- `durationMs` of a tool result (`ToolResultMessage.durationMs`, `NestedToolExecutionResult.durationMs`, nested slot summaries) is the span from the tool task's first run (`startedAt`) to its result on the Harness clock, hooks, parks, crash downtime, and reruns included, and results that never executed have one too. It was the time of the last `execute()` attempt. A record written before `startedAt` existed keeps the old measure.
28-- `pi.tool` is version 4 and `pi.generation` version 3; a database written by this version is not meant to be opened by an older Harness, which would block these tasks (`task_too_old`) and treat a sleep without `until` as due.
29-- Code-mode namespaces come from extensions, not name prefixes: `Extension.namespace` (`ToolNamespace`: `{ name, description, instructions? }`) groups the tools the extension brings (a tool several extensions name belongs to the first). `CodemodeNamespace`, its `prefix`, `namespaceOf` and `CodemodeToolOptions.namespaces` are removed, with no fallback. The `codemode` section lists every namespace of a selected extension, also one without tools yet (an MCP server waiting for sign-in), as `## <name>` and its one-line `description`, without tool counts, so the prompt stays the same when the extension's deferred tools appear; `instructions` are returned only by `describeNamespace()`, and `searchTools()` searches both. `namespacesOf(extensions)` (`@earendil-works/pi-durable/codemode`) maps tool names to their namespaces. Migration: move `namespaces: [{ name, description, prefix }]` into the extensions that bring those tools, as `namespace: { name, description, instructions? }`.
30-
31-### Added
32-
33-- Signals: `defineSignal({ name, version, schema, migrate? })` defines a typed JSON value delivered to a live task from outside with `harness.signal(taskId, token, key, value, context)` or `tx.signal()`, which answer `delivered`, `duplicate`, `invalid`, `closed`, or `not_found`. A value is kept in the task, also one that arrives before the sleep on its key, which then wakes at once; `readSignal(token, key, context)` on `TaskRuntime`, `HookApi`, and `ToolExecutionApi` reads it until the task ends, migrated to the token's version, or that the key expired. A key serves one wait: the wake marks it consumed.
34-- A sleep may wait for signals (`{ status: "sleeping", signals, until? }`) and ends at whichever comes first; a wait may use `policy: "any"` to resume once one task in `on` ends. A woken task reads why in `state.wake` (`WakeReason`: `time`, `expired`, `signal`, `tasks`), kept until it commits another checkpoint. Parked work holds no invocation, and `Harness.wake()` reports it inactive; a sleep without `until` adds no `at`.
35-- Tools that park: `execute()` may return `{ sleep: { checkpoint?, until?, signals? } }` or `{ wait: { checkpoint?, on, policy } }` and runs again, once woken, with `api.wake` and `api.checkpoint` set. The call holds no invocation meanwhile, its slot shows `sleeping` or `waiting` without output, and an invalid park ends it with an `invalid_park` result. `cancel(args, api, context)` cleans up the external work of a parked call that is aborted. Wrappers never park: a composite's park its base did not return is invalid.
36-- `executeTool(name, args, context, { wait: false })` starts or finds a nested call and returns `{ taskId, result(context) }`, so a tool can park on its nested calls; `api.createTask()` with a `key` returns the task the key names on a rerun or a later wake. After a wake, nested calls and tasks need explicit keys. A restart keeps the `abandonOnRestart` children of a call that was parked or not started yet.
37-- `SubmissionDraft.notify: { taskId, key }` delivers the built-in `SubmissionSettled` signal, the settled record, to a task when the submission settles, in the settling commit; a subagent tool can park until its child conversation answers.
38-- Gates: a `beforeTool` hook may return `{ sleep: { until?, signals? } }` to park a call before it runs; every wake, every registry publication, and every open run the whole `call` phase again, so the gates installed then decide. `HookApi.now()` reads the Harness clock.
39-- Hooks that start tasks: `afterTools` and `onYield` hooks may return `{ tasks }`, run as the generation's children. An `afterTools` task ends the run with `{ terminate: true }` (`AfterToolsDecision`) or answers it with a steer; `onYield` tasks decide whether an answer stands while the run's inputs stay open (`pi.live.run.yield`): once all are terminal, the first in creation order that completed with a valid `{ continue }` (`YieldDecision`) continues the run, unless a user message or a reset was queued meanwhile.
40-- Examples 38-46: signals, asking a person, a tool that waits for a webhook, a tool that polls, parallel nested calls, a subagent that waits, an approval gate, a review on yield, and an `afterTools` task that ends the run.
41-- `@earendil-works/pi-durable/images/fit` fits the images entering a conversation to its model's limits with any `ImageProcessor`, before they are stored, as the coding agent does: `createFitImagesExtension(processor)` is an `afterTool` hook for the results of every tool the model calls (MCP tools, code mode's `image()`), and `fitImage(bytes, mimeType, limits, processor)` and `fitImages(content, limits, processor)` fit a host's input before it is submitted. An image that cannot be prepared is left out with a note. `imageLimits(model)` (`/tools`) resolves a model's limits as `read` does. Example 47 shows both.
42-- `onAbort: "keep"` on an input submission keeps it queued through `Conversation.abort()` and abort cascades, as a failed run keeps its queue under `afterFailedRun: "keep"`: the next input places it and that run answers it. For input its sender cannot take back, such as another agent's message; `Submission.abort()` still withdraws it. The default, `"withdraw"`, settles it `unanswered` with reason `aborted` as before.
